display_name: Income Tax Ordinance s 66, separate calculation for spouses: who may claim it, where each spouse's income goes, property income under (b), the credit points s 66(c) gives in a separate calculation, and the common-source gate of (d)

run.method: one session working alone from BRIEF.md, per the encoding-a-subject skill; no sub-agents; no independent test pass

language.note: Every module starts @lang en; identifiers are English. Hebrew source strings are quoted in comments, copied from the deposited file.

source.note: Unofficial Hebrew Wikisource consolidation, as amended at retrieval. Hebrew is authoritative.

tax_years: From 2024. The last amendments to s 66 (תשפ״ג־6, תשפ״ד־3) apply from tax year 2024 per ITA circulars 2024-000012 and 2024-001090 (NOTES.md sections 3 and 7). From 0.2.0 every rule that takes the couple, or a tax year, refuses a tax year before 2024, because the earlier text is not in the source bundle; in 0.1.0 only three rules did (independent finding V-4, inventory 02-V4). Rules that take no year (one spouse, one item, a child's age, a provision) state the deposited text. A tax year after 2026 is a projection of the text as at 2026-10-06.
scope: s 66 in full: (a)(1)-(3), (b), (c)(1), (1A), (2), (3), (4) with (a), (a1), (4A), (5) with (a)-(c), (6), (d)(1)-(2); spent text ((c)(4)(b)-(d), (c)(5A), (e)) carried as inert stubs. Incorporated and encoded: the paragraphs of the s 1 definition of income from personal exertion (as an enumeration) and the s 40(b)(3) definitions of year of birth and year of majority. NOT encoded, taken as inputs or GIVENs: s 65 (the consolidated calculation is named as an outcome, not computed), s 64B (who is the registered spouse), the counts under ss 34, 35, 36, s 37's conditions, the value of a credit point (s 33A), the tax on income from personal exertion (ss 121 ff.), and the classification of income. From 0.2.0: s 48A, not encoded, is declined by name where it reaches the half point under s 36A that s 66(c)(4) gives (a woman who is a foreign worker), in row IL-01's words; s 66's own date edges (the (a)(1) five-year window, the (b) one-year and inheritance conditions) are the caller's. From 0.4.0: the forks F1, F6, F7, F8, F13, F14, F18 and F20 are switches that decline by default where their readings differ (Meng, SHRUG, 2026-10-08).

not_reviewed.note: No domain expert has read this encoding against the source. An independent test pass was run after deposit by fid-il-02 (commit 240a478: tests-independent.l4, DECIDED-ANSWERS.md, INDEPENDENT-FINDINGS.md); from 0.3.0 all 103 of its assertions hold (V-4 repaired in 0.2.0; E-4 by Meng's ruling on fork F19, SHRUG). No adversarial refuter has been run. The encoder's own assertions were written by the encoder (0.1.0) and the repair agent (0.2.0, 0.3.0), from the source, so they share their readings; 23 of them transcribe the Israel Tax Authority's own published tables.

expected_red.why: The independent tester's module. Six plain assertions (lines 241, 243, 244, 248, 250 = D-2, D-3, D-5, D-6; 259 = D-9) refuse under fork F1's default (Meng, SHRUG, 2026-10-08): their decided answers settle the (d)(1) conditions, not which F1 reading holds, so they were not re-pointed. Declared in check.sh (expected_refused 6). Five others (256, 300, 409, 416, 420) were re-pointed by name on the lead's authorisation of 2026-10-08 and pass; NOTE BY THE LEAD at the end of the file.

forks.F1: s 66(d)(1): the common-source gate read as on the COUPLE (subsection (a) does not apply to them at all), not on the common-source income alone, which s 64B(b) suggests. RULED by Meng on 2026-10-08 (SHRUG; BACKLOG IL-47, v0.4.0): one named switch, default DECLINE where the readings differ, every reading kept by name and tested; switch `section 66(d)(1) — the reading this row takes where a common source of income fails its conditions`. Reading (ii) reads a new MAYBE fact on `A common source of income`.
forks.F2: s 66(a)(1) proviso: a sum on commuting a pension (s 1 def. para (6)) is not a 'קיצבה'.
forks.F3: s 66(a)(2): equal non-zero incomes from personal exertion are answered by neither sentence; the encoding refuses. (0.4.0, 02-F3: class (b), already declined by name; left.)
forks.F4: s 66(a)(2): the comparison uses each spouse's whole income from personal exertion, including a pension the (a)(1) proviso keeps out of the separate calculation.
forks.F5: s 66(a)(3): 'ילדו' is the registered spouse's own child; a child of the other spouse alone is not reached.
forks.F6: s 66(a)(3): s 65's exception for assets from inheritance or bodily-injury compensation is not applied. RULED by Meng on 2026-10-08 (SHRUG; BACKLOG IL-47, v0.4.0): one named switch, default DECLINE where the readings differ, every reading kept by name and tested; switch `section 66(a)(3) — the reading this row takes of the exception in section 65`. The part from such assets is a new fact on the couple.
forks.F7: s 66(b) proviso: only the (a)(1) calculation of the spouse who is not registered is 'other income for which a separate calculation is made'; the registered spouse's claimed (b) income is always calculated alone. RULED by Meng on 2026-10-08 (SHRUG; BACKLOG IL-47, v0.4.0): one named switch, default DECLINE where the readings differ, every reading kept by name and tested; switch `section 66(b) — the reading this row takes of the proviso as to the registered spouse`.
forks.F8: s 66(c)(1A): not shut by the (d) gate, which names subsection (a) only. RULED by Meng on 2026-10-08 (SHRUG; BACKLOG IL-47, v0.4.0): one named switch, default DECLINE where the readings differ, every reading kept by name and tested; switch `section 66(c)(1A) — the reading this row takes where a common source of income fails subsection (d)(1)`.
forks.F9: s 66(c)(4)-(6): 'the woman' and 'the man' presuppose a mixed-sex couple; the encoding refuses for a couple of the same sex. (0.4.0, 02-F9: class (b), already declined by name; left.)
forks.F10: s 66(c): a credit provision it does not name (39A, 39B, 40A-40D, 44, 45, 46, ...) is refused, not defaulted. (0.4.0, 02-F10: class (b), already declined by name; left.)
forks.F11: s 66(c)(4)(a1): the birth-year election is the mother's and does not reach a step-mother's points under (4A).
forks.F12: s 66(c)(4A), (6): only a widowed partner's children count, not a divorced partner's.
forks.F13: s 66(c)(1A), (4), (5): the children's credit is capped at the tax on income from personal exertion; the ½ under s 36A is not. RULED by Meng on 2026-10-08 (SHRUG; BACKLOG IL-47, v0.4.0): one named switch, default DECLINE where the readings differ, every reading kept by name and tested; switch `section 66(c)(4)-(5) — the reading this row takes of the set-off of the children's credit`. A reading argument on the set-off rule.
forks.F14: s 66(a)(3) income stays on the registered spouse and does not move with the (a)(2) pool. RULED by Meng on 2026-10-08 (SHRUG; BACKLOG IL-47, v0.4.0): one named switch, default DECLINE where the readings differ, every reading kept by name and tested; switch `section 66(a)(2)-(3) — the reading this row takes of the children's income when the pool goes to the spouse who is not the registered spouse`. (inventory 02-F6)
forks.F15: s 66(a)(3): a child who turns 18 during the tax year is outside it.
forks.F16: s 66(c) governs both spouses' calculations once (a)(1) gives a separate calculation.
forks.F17: s 66(c)(4), (5): no maintenance or custody condition on the children.
forks.F18: s 66(c)(1A): 'בן זוג' includes the registered spouse. RULED by Meng on 2026-10-08 (SHRUG; BACKLOG IL-47, v0.4.0): one named switch, default DECLINE where the readings differ, every reading kept by name and tested; switch `section 66(c)(1A) — the reading this row takes as to the registered spouse`. (inventory 02-F8)
forks.F19: s 66(c)(4)(a1) at the vintage boundary (02-E4): a birth-year point elected for a child born before 2024 (in practice 2023) and carried into a 2024 calculation. RULED by Meng on 2026-10-08 (SHRUG; BACKLOG IL-38, v0.3.0): one named switch, `section 66(c)(4)(a1) — the reading this row takes for an election for a child born before 2024` in ito66-c-credit-points.l4, default `an election for a child born before 2024 is declined` (refusal: 'the text of section 66 this encoding holds does not decide a birth-year credit point elected for a child born before 2024'); the other reading, `an election for a child born before 2024 is carried by the text of the year of the calculation` (5½, the behaviour of 0.1.0-0.2.0), kept by name and tested. The election input carries no year.
forks.F20: s 66(c)(4) with s 36A (0.4.0; inventory 01-F1, shared with row IL-01's F1): whether the half point under s 36A needs the woman to be an Israeli resident. RULED by Meng on 2026-10-08 (SHRUG; BACKLOG IL-47, v0.4.0): one named switch, default DECLINE where the readings differ, every reading kept by name and tested; switch `section 66(c)(4) — the reading this row takes of section 36A on residence`. Mirrors IL-01 v0.3.0 (b64a3efb) and declines in its words, 'section 36A does not say whether a woman who is not an Israeli resident gets its half point'. Residence is a new fact on `A spouse`.
